messages:
maya (Support): hey @jonah saw your ticket — you're hitting embeddings endpoint and getting a dimension error? can you paste the exact error

jonah (Customer): yeah, quick paste: 
`400 Bad Request: embedding dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 768)`

maya (Support): ok thanks. couple quick checks: are you sending a single vector vs list, or accidentally sending nested arrays? also content-type header set to application/json?

jonah (Customer): sending from a numpy array -> json. here's the payload snippet: `{'input': np.array([0.1, 0.2, ...]).tolist()}` — i thought API accepted single vector

sam (Infra Eng): fyi the embeddings endpoint expects `input` to be a list of strings or list of token lists for batching; for vector ingestion (we don't ingest raw vectors) — but for similarity use-case some customers confuse client-side vs service expectation. Are you calling /embeddings or /embeddings/ingest?

jonah (Customer): calling /v1/embeddings with model: "open-embed-large". We used an open-source encoder offline and then tried to send vectors to us for indexing. The server responded with the dimension mismatch.

maya (Support): okay that explains. Our hosted embeddings endpoints accept text input and return vectors — they don't accept precomputed vectors. If you want to store vectors directly we have a separate ingest API (enterprise) or you need to store vectors in your DB. That mismatch error is because the server tried to interpret your array as a batch of strings (each char becoming small), or the model expected length 1536 and your vector is 768.

jonah (Customer): ohh, misunderstood. Is there any validation that gives a clearer hint? the 400 response is confusing

maya (Support): noted. for now, quick repro steps to confirm client-side shape: 1) try sending `{"input": ["hello world"]}` and see the returned vector length. 2) if you actually have vectors, call your internal storage path instead. 3) check Content-Type: `application/json; charset=utf-8` — some clients wrap np arrays as nested lists which turns into a shape like [[...]] and becomes a batch of 1 vector which still might mismatch.

jonah (Customer): trying step 1 now...

embed-bot: deploy log: embedding-model open-embed-large v1 loaded on shard-a3 (latency p50 12ms)

jonah (Customer): response for `{"input":["hello world"]}` -> works! got `embedding.length: 1536`

jonah (Customer): so yeah my array was 768 because I used a different encoder. How would you recommend handling storing those?

sam (Infra Eng): two paths: a) re-encode with chosen model to match our catalog (recommended for comparability), or b) if you must store your vectors, use metadata to tag them and run similarity locally. If you're mixing vector dims across items you'll get runtime confusion in downstream retrieval.

maya (Support): also note a common client mistake — sending JSON with `input` as a stringified JSON, e.g., `input: "[0.1, 0.2]"` which looks like a string and the server tries to treat it as a text prompt and returns text embedding (we don't interpret stringified vectors).

jonah (Customer): got it. For throughput: we were trying to batch 10k items by sending `input: [[...], [...]]` where inner lists were vectors. Would that ever work with embeddings endpoint?

sam (Infra Eng): nope, that endpoint expects list of text items. If there were an ingest endpoint it would accept list of vectors but with rate limits and chunking. For large bulk, chunk on client to ~256 items per request, parallelize, and respect 429 backoff. Also monitor tokenization if you send long texts — batch size should consider average token length.

maya (Support): extra debugging tips I usually share: 
- curl repro: 
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large","input":["hello world"]}'
- python snippet: 
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-large", input=["hello world"])\nprint(len(resp.data[0].embedding))
- confirm `input` is a list of strings, not nested numeric arrays

jonah (Customer): sweet, that solves my immediate problem. I'll re-run my pipeline to re-encode. two followups: can we detect and surface a clearer error if vector is sent? and is there a best-practice doc for bulk ingestion?

maya (Support): i'll escalate the error messaging to infra. filing internal ticket. for bulk ingestion best-practices we have a draft doc in product but let me link it: https://redwood.internal/docs/embeddings/bulk-ingest (internal). If you need immediate help with chunking I can drop a small script.

jonah (Customer): would appreciate the script. thanks!

sam (Infra Eng): tagging helper: @deploy-bot can we add a quick error message mapping when Content-Type is application/json and input contains only numeric arrays -> 400: "received numeric arrays; API expects text input for this endpoint. If you intended to upload precomputed vectors use ingest API or contact enterprise support."

deploy-bot: created ticket INF-2298 linking to this thread

maya (Support): thanks @sam. @jonah i'll DM the chunking script and leave this thread open until you confirm pipeline success :thumbsup:

jonah (Customer): thanks everyone — switching encoder now. will update once done. :rocket:
